_note: Portuguese tongue twisters (trava-línguas) for /trava-linguas. Several are well-known folk rhymes passed on orally (anonymous, in the form usual in Portugal; to verify the exact wording against a collection); the ones marked “new” in their hint were written for this course in the same spirit. Each one is first read out (slowly, then at speed), then the learner repeats it and gets points per word, the same scoring as /verificar-pronuncia. focus: sound ids from src/lib/ausspracheTipps.js. hint: what the twister means, in simple English. Ids are the old slot ids (content-plan §1.3); this set has 20 (quality over quantity). `audio` is set to true once public/audio/zungenbrecher/<id>-langsam.mp3 and <id>.mp3 exist; until then the browser voice (pt-PT where one is installed) reads them. mini (optional): an animal in the twister, so a small Mini-Crew sticker (src/lib/minis.js) sits on the card. mascot (optional): the same with an animal of the crew. dialect (optional): the same twister in a regional accent, voiced as <id>-<slug(dialect.name)>.mp3, only for listening and never scored; none in this set.

sentences.text: Três pratos de trigo para três tigres tristes.
sentences.hint: Three plates of wheat for three sad tigers. This is the best-known Portuguese tongue twister: say the r in tr- with one quick tap.

sentences.text: Pedro pagou pouco pelo pão preto.
sentences.hint: Pedro paid little for the black bread. New, written for this course. Say ou as o and the nasal ão with no clear n.

sentences.text: O peito do pé do Pedro é preto.
sentences.hint: The top of Pedro's foot is black. o peito do pé = the instep. Keep the open é of “é” and the short ei of “peito”.

sentences.text: A aranha arranha a rã. A rã arranha a aranha.
sentences.hint: The spider scratches the frog. The frog scratches the spider. nh is one sound, rr is the strong r, and rã is nasal.

sentences.text: O doce perguntou ao doce qual é o doce mais doce.
sentences.hint: The sweet asked the sweet which is the sweetest sweet. doce is both a sweet and an adjective (sweet). The c before e is a sharp s.

sentences.text: O pinto pia, a pia pinga; o pinto pinga e a pia pia.
sentences.hint: The chick cheeps, the basin drips; the chick drips and the basin cheeps. pia = (kitchen) sink, pinto = chick, and pia is also he or she cheeps. New, in the style of the traditional ones.

sentences.text: Se o papa papasse pão, o papa tudo papava.
sentences.hint: If the pope ate bread, the pope would eat everything. papar means to eat (informal, a bit playful); papa is the pope and also baby porridge.

sentences.text: O tempo perguntou ao tempo quanto tempo o tempo tem.
sentences.hint: Time asked time how much time time has. tempo means time and weather, and em is a nasal vowel with no clear m.

sentences.text: Quem a paca cara compra, paca cara pagará.
sentences.hint: Whoever buys the expensive paca (a large rodent) will pay an expensive paca. The accent on pagará puts the stress on the last syllable.

sentences.text: A vaca malhada foi molhada por outra vaca molhada e malhada.
sentences.hint: The spotted cow was wetted by another wet and spotted cow. malhada = spotted. lh is one sound, ou is o.

sentences.text: A Rita ria da rã e a rã ria da Rita.
sentences.hint: Rita laughed at the frog and the frog laughed at Rita. ria comes from rir (to laugh). New, written for this course. Every r at the start of a word is the strong r.

sentences.text: O vinho do vizinho vem do vinhedo.
sentences.hint: The neighbour's wine comes from the vineyard. New, written for this course. Three times the one sound nh.

sentences.text: O chefe achou a chave no chão da cozinha.
sentences.hint: The boss found the key on the kitchen floor. New, written for this course. ch is always sh, and chão is a nasal diphthong.

sentences.text: A Joana já viu a janela da igreja velha.
sentences.hint: Joana has already seen the window of the old church. New, written for this course. j is like the s in “measure”, and lh in velha is one sound.

sentences.text: Seis sacos de sal, seis cestos de salsa.
sentences.hint: Six sacks of salt, six baskets of parsley. New, written for this course. Final s is sh (seis, sacos), and an s at the start of a word is a sharp s.

sentences.text: Trazei três pratos num prato de trigo.
sentences.hint: Bring three plates on a plate of wheat. A variant of the famous one. trazei is the old plural form (vós), used in jokes and in the Bible.

sentences.text: Quando o Quim quiser, quero quatro quilos de queijo.
sentences.hint: When Quim wants, I want four kilos of cheese. New, written for this course. In que and qui the u is silent; in quando and quatro you say it.

sentences.text: Como queres que te queira, se quem eu quero que me queira não me quer como eu quero que me queira?
sentences.hint: How do you want me to love you, if the person I want to love me does not love me the way I want? querer = to want, and to love.

sentences.text: Cem cestos cheios de cebolas e cinco cebolas cheias de cheiro.
sentences.hint: A hundred baskets full of onions and five onions full of smell. New, written for this course. c before e or i is a sharp s, ch is sh.

sentences.text: O rato roeu a roupa do rei de Roma e a rainha com raiva rasgou o resto.
sentences.hint: The mouse gnawed the clothes of the king of Rome and the queen, in a rage, tore the rest. A well-known folk twister: every r at the start of a word is the strong r.
